text:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary rollout started for rate-limiter v2.1.0 -> 10% traffic in eu-west-1. ID=deploy/rl-v2.1.0/2028-03-10

sam: seeing a spike in 429s from the proxy logs against api.redwood.host, started around 2801234580. Not sure if canary noise yet. :eyes:

oncall-bot: Pager: P0 - Canary rate-limiter deployment increasing 429s above SLO (api 95th > 200ms and 429 uptick). Paging on-call: sam, maria.

maria: acked. I'm looking at the rate-limiter metrics and exemptions table. Quick telemetry: rate_limit_rejections{env="prod",region="eu-west-1"} jumped x8 at 2801234582.

kevin: fyi support queue is starting to get messages about timeouts for third-party integrations, possibly retries. Tagging @support-lead

support-lead: we have 12 incoming support tickets mentioning "quota" or "throttled" in the last 5m. Customers affected include two mid-market customers on dedicated and several hosted small apps. Triage in progress.

sam: grep of the exemption sync logs shows missing exemptions for internal tokens after the migration step during deploy. Log snippet:
```
2028-03-10T12:03:01Z ERROR exemptions_sync: failed to apply exemptions: KeyError('service_token_id')
2028-03-10T12:03:01Z INFO exemptions_sync: rollback to previous snapshot
```

jess: that aligns. Canary included a change to the exemptions schema (nullable -> required) and the migration ran only on primary DB, not the read replica the sync job uses. The sync job masked the mismatch and then failed, clearing the in-memory exemption cache.

maria: mitigation plan: 1) pause canary (hold new rollouts), 2) flip kill-switch to force fallback to legacy rate limiter config, 3) trigger immediate restore of exemptions from last snapshot, 4) rollback if needed. Who can flip the kill-switch?

sam: I can flip it. Command: `kubectl -n redwood exec deploy/rl-config-updater -- /bin/sh -c "./flip_flag --name=rl-use-legacy --value=true"`

oncall-bot: Action started by sam at 2801234620: flipping rl-use-legacy -> true

deploy-bot: Canary paused. Traffic weight set to 0%.

kevin: support-lead, share a quick CS stub for impacted customers: "We're investigating elevated throttling due to a deployment in our rate-limiting layer. We've paused the rollout and are restoring normal behavior. Updates in ~15 minutes."

support-lead: posted to customer portal and opened priority cases for those two mid-market customers.

maria: starting restore from snapshot: `exemptions-restore --from s3://redwood-backups/exemptions/2028-03-10T11:58:00.json --apply --dry-run=false`

ops: observed fast recovery of exemption cache on main nodes. Cache miss rate dropping. Metrics: rate_limit_rejections back to baseline within ~90s of flip.

sam: rolling reconciliation job now running to ensure read replicas have schema/tombstone parity. Command run: `pg_dump -s | psql replica` then `service exemptions-sync restart`

product-lead: what was customer impact window? We should prepare a postmortem and comms.

support-lead: initial window from 2801234582 -> 2801234635 (≈53s of elevated 429s for some tenants, retries caused downstream errors). Two customers reported degraded UX, no data loss.

jess: root cause: migration + sync ordering bug. Migration assumed replicas were migrated before sync job, but deploy ordering allowed sync to run against a partial migration state which resulted in clearing in-memory exemptions.

maria: status update: exemptions restored, legacy flag on, canary remains paused pending rollback verification. I recommend rollback of rl-v2.1.0 to avoid reintroduction until we have migration fix and canary safeguards.

sam: initiating rollback: `redwood deploy rollback --service rate-limiter --to-tag v2.0.7 --region eu-west-1`

oncall-bot: Rollback command accepted; monitoring rollback progress.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed to v2.0.7 in eu-west-1 at 2801234700. No additional traffic routed to v2.1.0.

ops: verify: 5xx/429s at baseline; p95 latency back to normal. Killswitch remains on as we coordinate a safer re-deploy.

kevin: can we get an ETA for root-cause fix and safe re-release?

jess: patch is small: change sync job to verify schema version and block until migrations are applied on all DB endpoints, plus add defensive checks. We'll run a test deploy in staging and a canary with 1% and automatic rollback on exemption mismatch. ETA 4–6 hours.

product-lead: please log affected customers and timeline for incident report. We'll send a consolidated field notice after RCA.

support-lead: done — stub created and case notes updated.

maria: handoff: I'm on-call for the next 30m to watch metrics; handover to kevin after. If anything re-spikes, flip rl-use-legacy -> true remains the immediate mitigation.

sam: leaving notes in incident channel and runbook updated with new checklist: verify replicas before sync, sanity-check exemptions cache after migration, automatic kill-switch on 3x baseline 429s in 60s.

ops: post-incident, we should add a canary test that simulates missing exemptions to validate fallback behavior.

support-lead: customers notified: two affected customers offered a one-day credit; smaller tenants received status updates. No major SLA breaches expected but tracking.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 2801234740. Follow-up: create postmortem, patch and redeploy with stricter canary controls, and add automated exemption integrity check. :white_check_mark:

sam: thanks everyone — quick coordination saved a lot of customer pain. Closing thread after postmortem. :hammer:
